title: Adverbial clauses of time (2)
summary: Тонкости придаточных времени: as soon as, the moment, once, by the time, until, since, every time, а также no sooner ... than и hardly ... when; времена в таких придаточных.
ru:
## Что вы уже знаете и что здесь нового
С **when, while, before, after** вы знакомы. Здесь — более тонкие союзы и конструкции, которые делают речь точнее: **as soon as, the moment, once, by the time, until, since, every time**, а также книжные **no sooner ... than** и **hardly ... when**.

## Моментальная последовательность
Когда одно действие следует за другим почти без паузы, используем **as soon as, the moment (that), the instant (that), once**. В британском английском также **immediately** и **directly** как союзы.
> **The moment** she saw the invoice, she called the accountant. — В ту секунду, как она увидела счёт, она позвонила бухгалтеру.
> **Once** you've signed the form, we can start. — Как только вы подпишете форму, мы можем начинать.
> He phoned **immediately** he got the results. (BrE) — Он позвонил сразу же, как получил результаты.
Между **as soon as** и **once** есть оттенок: **once** подчёркивает, что первое действие должно быть полностью завершено (условие + время).

## No sooner ... than и hardly ... when
Это формальная конструкция с **инверсией** (вспомогательный глагол перед подлежащим), обычно с past perfect в первой части:
> **No sooner had** we landed **than** the storm broke. — Едва мы приземлились, как разразилась буря.
> **Hardly had** the speech ended **when** the crowd began to cheer. — Едва речь закончилась, как толпа начала аплодировать.
После **no sooner** — только **than**; после **hardly / scarcely** — **when** (или **before**). Форма ~~hardly ... than~~ в строгом стиле считается ошибкой, хотя в речи встречается.

## Будущее в придаточных времени
После **when, as soon as, until, before, after, once, by the time** будущее выражается **present simple** или **present perfect** (если важно, что действие завершено). **Will** там не ставим.
> I'll send the report **as soon as I finish** the last chapter.
> Don't sign anything **until you've read** the whole contract. — Ничего не подписывайте, пока не прочтёте весь договор.
> **By the time** you read this, I'll have left. — К тому времени, как вы это прочтёте, я уже уеду.
Но если **when** вводит не придаточное времени, а вопрос или дополнение, **will** возможен:
> I don't know **when** the committee **will** announce its decision. — Не знаю, когда комитет объявит решение.

## by the time, until, since
- **by the time** = «к тому моменту, когда»: речь о крайнем сроке, а не о длительности. By the time we arrived, the shop **had closed**.
- **until / till** = «до тех пор, пока (не)»: действие длится вплоть до момента. Till менее формально. Для акцента: **It wasn't until** midnight **that** the guests left. — Лишь в полночь гости ушли.
- **since**: после него past simple (точка отсчёта) или present perfect: **It's ten years since** I last saw him. / She has lived here **since** she was a student.

## every time, the next time
Сочетания **every / each / the first / the last / the next time** сами работают как союзы, **предлоги не нужны**:
> **The next time** you visit, bring your photos. — В следующий раз, когда приедешь, привези фото.
> **Every time** I hear that song, I think of Lisbon.
- ~~At the next time you come~~ → **The next time** you come
- ~~The next time when you come~~ → The next time you come

## Типичные ошибки
- ~~I'll tell you as soon as I will know.~~ → as soon as I **know**.
- ~~Hardly had I sat down than the phone rang.~~ → Hardly had I sat down **when** the phone rang.
- ~~Since I moved here, I didn't see snow.~~ → I **haven't seen** snow.
- ~~I'm waiting since two o'clock.~~ → I've been waiting **since** two o'clock.
en:
## What is new here
You already know **when, while, before** and **after**. This unit adds more precise time linkers: **as soon as, the moment, once, by the time, until, since, every time**, and the formal patterns **no sooner ... than** and **hardly ... when**.

## Immediate sequence
When one action follows another almost at once, use **as soon as, the moment (that), the instant (that)** or **once**. In British English **immediately** and **directly** can also be conjunctions.
> **The moment** she saw the invoice, she called the accountant.
> **Once** you've signed the form, we can start.
> He phoned **immediately** he got the results. (BrE)
**Once** stresses that the first action must be fully finished.

## No sooner ... than and hardly ... when
These are formal and use **inversion**, usually with the past perfect in the first part:
> **No sooner had** we landed **than** the storm broke.
> **Hardly had** the speech ended **when** the crowd began to cheer.
**No sooner** goes with **than**; **hardly / scarcely** go with **when** (or **before**). ~~Hardly ... than~~ is considered incorrect in careful writing.

## Future meaning in time clauses
After **when, as soon as, until, before, after, once, by the time** we use the **present simple** or **present perfect** (for a completed action), not **will**.
> I'll send the report **as soon as I finish** the last chapter.
> Don't sign anything **until you've read** the whole contract.
> **By the time** you read this, I'll have left.
But when **when** introduces a question or a noun clause, **will** is possible:
> I don't know **when** the committee **will** announce its decision.

## by the time, until, since
- **by the time** gives a deadline: By the time we arrived, the shop **had closed**.
- **until / till** means up to a moment; **It wasn't until** midnight **that** the guests left.
- **since** takes the past simple or the present perfect: **It's ten years since** I last saw him. / She has lived here **since** she was a student.

## every time, the next time
Phrases like **every / each / the first / the last / the next time** work as conjunctions on their own, with **no preposition**:
> **The next time** you visit, bring your photos.
> **Every time** I hear that song, I think of Lisbon.
- ~~At the next time you come~~ → **The next time** you come

## Common mistakes
- ~~as soon as I will know~~ → as soon as I **know**
- ~~Hardly had I sat down than ...~~ → ... **when** the phone rang
- ~~Since I moved here, I didn't see snow.~~ → I **haven't seen** snow.
structure:
## Союзы и конструкции
| Форма | Значение | Пример |
|---|---|---|
| as soon as / the moment / once | сразу после | Once you've paid, you'll get a link. |
| by the time | к тому моменту (срок) | By the time I got home, they'd gone. |
| until / till | вплоть до | Wait until I call. |
| since | с тех пор как | It's a year since we met. |
| every / next / last time | каждый / в следующий раз | The next time you call, ask for Sam. |

## Формулы
> **No sooner** + had + подлежащее + V3 + **than** + past simple
> No sooner had she left **than** it started to rain.

> **Hardly / Scarcely** + had + подлежащее + V3 + **when / before** + past simple
> Hardly had she left **when** it started to rain.

> **It wasn't until** + время + **that** + past simple
> It wasn't until 2019 **that** the firm made a profit.

## Времена в придаточных времени
| Главная часть | Придаточное | Пример |
|---|---|---|
| will / команда | present simple | I'll call when I arrive. |
| will / команда | present perfect (завершённость) | Call me once you've arrived. |
| past simple | past simple / past perfect | The moment he came in, we left. |

exercises.title: Времена в придаточных времени
exercises.instruction: Поставьте глагол в скобках в подходящую форму (если допустимы present simple и present perfect — укажите любую).
exercises.example: I'll call you as soon as the plane (land). → **lands**

items.text: I'll call you as soon as the plane {{lands|has landed}}.
We can't start until everyone {{has arrived|arrives}}.
By the time you read this email, I {{will have left|'ll have left}} the country.
Once the building {{has been inspected|is inspected}}, the tenants can move in.
The moment she {{walked}} in, everybody stopped talking.
I don't know when the committee {{will announce|is going to announce|'ll announce|is announcing}} its decision.
Don't sign anything until {{you've read|you have read|you read}} the whole contract.
No sooner had we sat down {{than}} the music started.
Hardly had the lecture begun {{when|before}} the projector failed.
It wasn't {{until|till}} last year that the museum opened to the public.
We have known each other {{since|ever since}} we were children.
{{The next time|Next time}} you visit, please bring the documents.
Every {{time}} I hear that song, I think of Lisbon.
I'll be waiting {{until|till}} the last guest has gone.
{{By the time}} the ambulance arrived, the crowd had dispersed.

items.q: ___ the sun went down, the temperature dropped sharply.
items.why: **As** показывает два параллельных процесса, развивающихся вместе; until здесь не подходит по смыслу, а during — предлог, после него не может стоять предложение.

items.q: I'll text you as soon as I ___ at the hotel.
items.why: После as soon as будущее выражается present simple: **arrive**.

items.q: By the time we got to the cinema, the film ___.
items.why: Действие произошло **до** момента прибытия в прошлом — past perfect.

items.q: Give me a call when you ___ ready.
items.why: В придаточном времени после when — present simple, не will (call me when... = «позвони, когда будешь готов»).

items.q: No sooner had she put down the phone ___ it rang again.
items.why: **No sooner** сочетается только с **than**; when — с hardly / scarcely.

items.q: ___ you finish the first draft, send it to me.
items.why: **Once** = как только (первое действие завершено); during — предлог, а не союз.

items.q: It's ten years ___ I last saw her.
items.why: Модель **It's ... since + past simple** — «прошло ... лет с тех пор, как».

items.q: ___ I see him, he asks me for money.
items.why: **Every time** — самостоятельный союз, без артикля и предлога.

exercises.title: Найдите верное предложение
exercises.instruction: Только одно предложение в каждом пункте правильное.

options: As soon as she will call, I'll tell her.
As soon as she calls, I'll tell her.
As soon as she called, I'll tell her.
items.why: Будущее в придаточном времени — present simple.

options: The next time when you visit us, stay longer.
At the next time you visit us, stay longer.
The next time you visit us, stay longer.
items.why: The next time уже работает как союз — when и предлог лишние.

options: It wasn't until midnight that the guests left.
It wasn't until midnight when the guests left.
It wasn't till midnight that did the guests leave.
items.why: Модель **It wasn't until ... that** + обычный порядок слов.

options: Hardly I had sat down when the phone rang.
Hardly had I sat down when the phone rang.
Hardly had I sat down than the phone rang.
items.why: После hardly — инверсия (had I) и союз when; than в строгом стиле неверно.

options: I've been waiting since two hours.
I've been waiting since two o'clock.
I've been waiting for two o'clock.

items.q: By the time you get this message, I ___.
items.why: К будущему моменту действие уже завершится — future perfect.

items.q: Once the form ___, you can't change your answers.
items.why: Пассив в present simple: форма «подаётся»; will после once не используем.

exercises.title: Перепишите предложения
exercises.instruction: Перепишите предложение, используя слова в скобках. Смысл сохраните.

items.prompt: As soon as he sat down, the meeting began. → No sooner ...
answers: No sooner had he sat down than the meeting began.

answers: Hardly had the curtain risen when the audience fell silent.
Hardly had the curtain risen before the audience fell silent.

answers: By the time we reached the station, the train had already left.

exercises.title: Напишите о себе
exercises.instruction: Ответьте полными предложениями, используя союзы времени из юнита.

items.prompt: What will you do as soon as you finish your studies or work today?
items.sample: As soon as I finish work today, I'll go for a long walk.

items.prompt: Describe a moment when something happened immediately after something else (no sooner ... than).
items.sample: No sooner had I left the house than it started to pour with rain.

items.prompt: What do you always do every time you travel by train?
items.sample: Every time I travel by train, I buy a coffee and read a book.

items.prompt: Tell about something you could not do until a certain age (It wasn't until ... that).
items.sample: It wasn't until I was twenty that I learned to swim properly.
